name: Boot Log Timeline
blurb: a boot log or systemd-analyze output split into stages on a timeline, slowest first
intro: Lays a boot on one time axis from what the log itself says: U-Boot's bootstage report or host timestamps for the bootloader, printk times, initcall_debug initcall and probe durations for the kernel, and systemd's Starting/Started lines or systemd-analyze output for userspace. It ranks the slowest items, finds the silent gaps and names the usual causes.

examples.title: systemd-analyze time, critical-chain and blame from a gateway

input.log:
root@gateway:~# systemd-analyze time
Startup finished in 3.012s (kernel) + 11.284s (userspace) = 14.297s
multi-user.target reached after 11.201s in userspace
root@gateway:~# systemd-analyze critical-chain
The time when unit became active or started is printed after the "@" character.
The time the unit took to start is printed after the "+" character.

multi-user.target @11.201s
└─docker.service @7.902s +3.297s
  └─network-online.target @7.889s
    └─NetworkManager-wait-online.service @2.431s +5.456s
      └─NetworkManager.service @2.101s +318ms
        └─dbus.service @2.071s
          └─basic.target @2.052s
            └─sockets.target @2.051s
              └─docker.socket @2.030s +20ms
                └─sysinit.target @2.021s
                  └─systemd-udev-settle.service @812ms +1.203s
                    └─systemd-udev-trigger.service @502ms +301ms
                      └─systemd-journald.socket @431ms
                        └─-.mount @398ms
                          └─-.slice @398ms
root@gateway:~# systemd-analyze blame
5.456s NetworkManager-wait-online.service
3.297s docker.service
1.203s systemd-udev-settle.service
 842ms dev-mmcblk0p2.device
 611ms containerd.service
 318ms NetworkManager.service
 301ms systemd-udev-trigger.service
 244ms systemd-journald.service
 190ms systemd-timesyncd.service
 122ms systemd-logind.service
  98ms systemd-fsck-root.service
  71ms systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service
  44ms systemd-remount-fs.service
  20ms docker.socket

usage: Give log as the text of one boot (serial console, dmesg, journalctl -b -o short-monotonic, or systemd-analyze time/critical-chain/blame output), gap in ms and top. It returns the stage totals (firmware, bootloader, kernel, userspace, like systemd-analyze time), the slowest items across bootloader stages, initcalls, driver probes and units, the silent gaps with a likely cause, and warnings for bootdelay, failed or deferred probes, failed units and known slow units. Use it to find where boot time goes and what to fix first.
sources: Linux init/main.c do_one_initcall_debug ("calling"/"initcall ... returned ... after N usecs") and drivers/base/dd.c really_probe_debug ("probe with driver ... returned ... after N usecs")
Linux Documentation/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.txt: initcall_debug, printk.time, rootwait, quiet, loglevel
U-Boot common/bootstage.c bootstage_report (Timer summary in microseconds, Mark / Elapsed / Stage) and include/bootstage.h
systemd src/analyze (time, blame, critical-chain: @ = activating minus userspace start, + = activation time) and systemd-analyze(1)
